Canopy tents go by a lot of names: screen houses, outdoor canopies, camping shelters, day tents, camping gazebos, patio shelters, portable shelters, and (our favorite) portable gazebos.

s.d: (Ireland, derogatory) a gaudy, incongruous, or flimsy structure or object
x: 'I'll thank ye tell me what they mean by that old gazabo on the top of the market-place,' said she, in a burst of ridicule fit to have brought the old tower down.
There was no garden attached to this tenement, nor was there even a good yard. People looked at it in passing by and called it a gazebo, a rattle-trap, a castle rack-rent.

gazelle.e: Unadapted borrowing from Middle French gazelle, from Old French gazel, from Arabic غَزَال (ḡazāl).

s.d: small swift graceful antelope of Africa and Asia having lustrous eyes
An antelope of either of the genera Gazella (mostly native to Africa), Procapra (native to Asia), Eudorcas, or Nanger, capable of running at high speeds for long periods.
x: “One does not judge the gazelle by the lions that attack it,” replied Tarzan.

s.d: (figuratively) To leap like a gazelle.
x: The biplane gazelled into the air.
When I started off [spacewalking] I didn’t run straight away—I started at a fairly fast walk, three or four miles an hour—but by the end I was jogging, well, gazelling, at almost six miles an hour.

s.d: (figuratively) To go fast; to speed; to rush.
x: Nadezhda and I biked over together, me dressed in colonial whites, trundling along with other cyclists gazelling by me on both sides […]
I actually heard the air move as about five people gazelled towards Lord Mandelson to try to stop another of his ill-timed leaks.

s.d: old breed of tall swift keen-eyed hunting dogs resembling greyhounds; from Egypt and southwestern Asia
Synonym of Saluki.

gazette.e: Borrowed from French gazette, from Italian gazzetta, from Venetan gazeta, from gazeta dele novità (literally “a gazeta (halfpenny) of news”), named for the cost (one gazeta) of the newspaper. Compare penny dreadful, dime novel. See gazzetta for more.

s.d: a newspaper or official journal
A newspaper; a printed sheet published periodically.
An official periodical publication published by a government containing legal and state notices, and in some cases, legislations, subsidiary legislations and bills.
publish in a gazette
(UK) To announce the status of (someone) in an official gazette; this pertained to both appointments and bankruptcies.
x: Benjamin had already been gazetted captain and Kopp was in process of being gazetted major.

s.d: a journalist who writes for a gazette
a geographical dictionary (as at the back of an atlas)
(archaic, historical) A person who writes for a gazette or newspaper; a journalist; (specifically) a journalist engaged by a government.
x: Mount novv to Gallo-belgicus: Appeare / As deepe as a States-man, as a Gazettier.
Did I tell you I have made Ford Gazetteer, with two hundred pounds a year salary, besides perquisites.

s.d: (obsolete) A gazette, a newspaper.

s.d: A dictionary or index of geographical locations.
x: This is the first volume of a gazetteer which is now being published. It may be looked upon as the very latest authority.

s.d: A similar descriptive list (often alphabetical) of information on other subjects.
x: Unlike other prehistoric processes, there is no comprehensive gazetteer of radiocarbon dates for the entire Bell Beaker phenomenon apart from a few high-quality regional datasets[…].

s.d: Synonym of gazette (“to announce the status of (someone) in an official gazette”).
x: [A]s an old friend I've got one favour to beg and to request to be granted. […] Why, when you've been gazetteered as Sir Robert and Lady Smugglefuss, that I shall be the first to be honoured with a visit.
But the change was at hand, and two new major-generals and six brigadier-generals were gazetteered to the anxious country.

s.d: (archaic) To report about (someone) in a gazette or newspaper.
x: Patience, it will be our turn by and by, we shall have the honour of being Gazetteered in our place, at least I expect a whole paragraph in the 'Evening Post' for my own share.

s.d: To describe the geography of (a country or other place) in a gazetteer (etymology 2, noun sense 1).

s.d: a very large indefinite number (usually hyperbole)
x: there were millions of flies

gazpacho.e: From Spanish gazpacho, perhaps via Mozarabic *gazpelağo from Latin gazophylacium (“treasure-chest in a church”), alluding to the diversity of its contents. Alternatively, related to Spanish caspicias (“remnants”).

s.d: a soup made with chopped tomatoes and onions and cucumbers and peppers and herbs; served cold
(uncountable) A cold soup of Spanish origin, made with olive oil, vinegar, bread and raw vegetables such as tomatoes, garlic, onion, cucumber and sweet peppers.
x: Seville is the home of gazpacho, a delicious cold soup of cucumber, tomato, and miscellaneous garnishings.

s.d: (Australia, UK) The act of gazumping.
(US, dated, slang) An automobile.
x: "Phoney" Thorpe, '06, and "Shorty" Winchester, '01, have been driving their "90 HP Gazumps" through the wilds of New Jersey, but otherwise keeping on the job.
Go out and hire the finest gazump that ever burned benzine.

s.d: A politician who takes bribes.

(UK) To swindle; to extort.
(Australia, UK) To buy a property by bidding more than the price of an existing, accepted offer.
(Australia, UK) To trump or preempt; to reap the benefit underhandedly from a situation that someone else has worked to create.
